description: German vocabulary register audit list. 'formal' = Amtsdeutsch/Schriftsprache item stiff or dead in conversation; 'preferred' = what German speakers actually say. Deck defaults: du/Sie by context, Perfekt in dialogue (sein/haben/modals keep Präteritum). Severity: 'high' = dead in speech, swap wherever it appears in conversational cards; 'medium' = written-leaning, swap in beginner content. See docs/german-register-policy.md.

dead_in_speech.rationale: Written-German verbs, connectors, and tense usage that never occur in conversation.

entries.note: «sich zum Bahnhof begeben» is announcement/officialese; speech says gehen or fahren. Medical «sich in Behandlung begeben» is genre language — exempt when quoted.
erhalten is standard in letters and forms; conversation says bekommen (neutral) or kriegen (colloquial). Only flag in dialogue cards.
Amtsdeutsch; in speech it reads as corporate parody.
«der Mann, welcher dort steht» → «der Mann, der dort steht». Question-word welcher («Welcher Bus?») is everyday — exempt.

entries.formal: Präteritum of ordinary verbs in dialogue (ich aß, er kaufte)
entries.preferred: Perfekt (ich habe gegessen, er hat gekauft)
entries.note: Written-narrative tense. Exempt: sein, haben, modals, werden, es gab, and Q4 narrative/reading cards taught as such.
